cards.title: Introduction to Data Structures
cards.content:
Data structures are ways of organizing and storing data efficiently in Python.

Python provides built-in data structures like Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, and Sets.

options.text: Lists are immutable and tuples are mutable.
Lists are mutable and tuples are immutable.
Both lists and tuples are immutable.
Both lists and tuples are mutable.

cards.title: Python Dictionaries
cards.content:
Dictionaries store data in key: value pairs.

my_dict = {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}
print(my_dict["name"])  # Output: Alice

cards.title: Big-O Efficiency in Python
cards.content:
Understanding time complexity helps write performant code.

  • List lookup by index: O(1)
  • List search (in operator): O(n)
  • Dictionary lookup/insertion: O(1) average

items.text: Initialize an empty list to act as a stack
Use append() to push an item onto the stack
Check the top of the stack using negative indexing (stack[-1])
Use pop() to remove the top item from the stack

cards.title: Data Structures Summary
cards.content:
Choosing the right data structure is crucial for writing efficient Python applications.

Review the complexities and properties before building large-scale systems.
